chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah, from Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn al-Saghir, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام. And Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Faddal, from some of his men, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Jibra'il عليه السلام descended upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and said: 'O Muhammad, your Lord conveys peace to you and says: I have indeed forbidden the Fire for the loins that brought you forth, the womb that carried you, and the lap that cared for you. So the loins are the loins of your father Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the womb that carried you is Aminah bint Wahb, and as for the lap that cared for you, it is the lap of Abu Talib.'
And in the narration of Ibn Faddal: 'And Fatimah bint Asad.'

key_terms.أَبِي طَالِبٍ: Abu Talib, identified here as the one who cared for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.السَّلَامَ: peace and greeting conveyed from Allah to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.النَّارَ: the Fire, meaning punishment in Hell
key_terms.بَطْنٍ: the womb that carried the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibra'il, the angel who descended with the divine message
key_terms.حِجْرٍ: the lap or protective care under which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was raised
key_terms.صُلْبٍ: the paternal loins or lineage through which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله came
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ بِنْتِ أَسَدٍ: Fatimah bint Asad, mentioned in one version of the report

ai.seo_question: Which relatives and caretakers of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله are mentioned in the hadith as being forbidden to the Fire?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Jibra'il عليه السلام brought salutations from Allah to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and conveyed that the Fire was forbidden for those directly connected to his birth and care. It identifies his father Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, his mother Aminah bint Wahb, and Abu Talib, with another version also mentioning Fatimah bint Asad. The report highlights the honored status of the Prophet's immediate family and caretakers.
